answer: A harbor master does not trust every ship that sails in from the open ocean: entry is granted only to vessels vouched for by captains already anchored inside, and each vouch puts the voucher's own reputation on the line. A sybil fleet can copy hulls all day, but without genuine links into the trusted graph it stays outside the reef — one fake identity costs nothing, yet a hundred fakes still earn zero trust, because trust flows through real relationships, not headcount.
